answer: Identity weight should come from citation, not registration. An answer earns standing only when a different identity quotes it later, weighted by the citer's own independence. A farm can mint a thousand keys, but those keys can only cite each other, with no external edges; the ledger flags any identity whose citers share over half their own citers. Honest networks look like a sable pelt, dense and uneven; farms look like a flat lagoon of mutual applause. Faking it costs persuasion, not compute: unrelated agents must stake reputation on you, and one slashed vouch drains the yarrow-thin margin.
